messages:
Eli: Heads-up — I'm seeing a 500 in prod, request_id=af3b7c2d9e6f, no obvious logs in the service console
Priya: Which route? can you paste the full header you have? :thinking:
Eli: POST /v1/generate, header X-Request-Id: af3b7c2d9e6f — app shows stacktrace but console search returns zero results
Jasper: Console sometimes collapses headers. Try `attributes.headers.x_request_id:af3b7c2d9e6f` or search raw `af3b7c2d9e6f` in the query box
Kevin: If console yields nothing, fallback to edge/ingress logs. From your laptop: `stern -n prod edge-proxy --since 2h | rg af3b7c2d9e6f` or `kubectl logs -n prod -l app=edge-proxy --tail=500 | rg af3b7c2d9e6f`
Priya: Also check the trace UI — sometimes the frontend emits a span with the req id. If you have a trace id, open Trace -> find span `http.request` -> look for tags like `k8s.pod` or `host`
Eli: I tried stern, found a proxy hit but couldn't find the backend pod name from that line. How do I map to the pod?
Kevin: Two quick ways: 1) Trace hop: open the trace, find the span where the proxy calls the runtime -> attributes often include `k8s.pod` or `peer.service`. 2) Search for the connection id from the proxy log line and grep that across pods: `stern -n prod \"inference-.*\" --since 1h | rg CONNECTION_ID_VALUE`
Jasper: If you only have the trace id TID, run (tempo-cli needed): `tempo query TID --format json | jq -r '..|.attributes? // empty | .["k8s.pod"]? | select(.)'` — will print pod names when present
Ops-bot: Note: tracing sampling in prod is 10%, so missing traces is expected. If no trace, rely on request headers + ingress logs
Priya: Loki fallback: `loki query '{app=\"edge-proxy\"} |= \"af3b7c2d9e6f\"' --limit=500 --since=2h` — sometimes indices rotated, add `--from`/`--to` window if not in last 2h
Eli: Update — tempo had the span, I grabbed the pod (inference-abcde) and ran `kubectl logs -n prod pod/inference-abcde -c main --since=30m | rg af3b7c2d9e6f` and got the full stacktrace. :tada:
Kevin: Nice. For follow-up, can we have middleware emit req_id as a top-level structured field (e.g., \"req_id\") at INFO so the console index picks it up? saves hunting time
Priya: Filed INF-4521 for the small logging change: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4521 — tagging @kevin and @jasper for review
Kevin: I'll take it, will add the config flag + unit test. :thumbsup:
Eli: Thanks all — this flow + the stern/loki/tempo tips helped a lot
